title: Steady Progress Beats Stagnation: Mutual Aid of Foundation and Conventional Models in Mixed Domain Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: A LoRA-tuned foundation model and a conventional U-Net co-train on mixed-domain unlabelled data. The pseudo-label is a per-image weighted ensemble set by self-confidence and mutual agreement: the FM leads early, the CNN corrects its over-confident errors later, and a consensus-divergence consistency loss ties them.
adaptation: FM = SAM2 Hiera or DINOv2-B + LoRA with a mask head, which supplies context such as the half-cut layout. Conventional model = house U-Net++, which supplies thin-crack resolution. The mixed-domain unlabelled set = pool (CSIR/ARTS, mono, multi, half-cells), with labelled cells from 5 sources.
min_experiment: Arm: SynFoC pair with the CNN branch evaluated, 3 seeds. Baseline: PF house. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU, clean-49 crack IoU. Kill: E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03 and inactive IoU gain < +0.03.
evidence: R: four multi-domain medical datasets (Prostate, Fundus, M&Ms, BUSI) at few labels; Prostate Dice +10.31% over prior methods.
prior_overlap: Partial. The SSL row ran on ResNet-34 only, and BRIEF lists SSL with foundation-model teachers as open. CPS (also co-training) was run at 5% only.
